notes: Access tier 1 (direct HTTP fetch via curl, SSR HTML) succeeded fully; no Playwright/Chrome needed. robots.txt (https://vaaree.com/robots.txt, generic User-agent: * rule, no Claude-specific disallow) explicitly allows /collections/ and /sitemap*.xml; site is a Next.js/Shopify-style storefront on vaaree.com (www redirects to bare domain). Discovery method: fetched sitemap.xml -> sitemap_collections_1.xml + sitemap_collections_2.xml (3208 total collection URLs) and keyword-searched the full list for Christmas/Xmas/Diwali/Deepavali/Halloween/Holi/Rakhi/Raksha Bandhan/Navratri/Dussehra/Eid/Ganesh/Janmashtami/Pongal/Onam/Durga/Karwa Chauth/Sankranti/Baisakhi/New Year/Valentine/Easter/Thanksgiving/Mother's Day/Father's Day/Festive/Festival/Holiday terms; cross-checked against the homepage's rendered nav/mega-menu link set (108 /collections/ links) which did NOT surface a dedicated Diwali/Christmas/Festival dropdown, meaning these seasonal collections are SEO/landing pages reachable via sitemap and direct URL rather than primary nav - still evaluated under the genuine-PLP test since site's own title/H1/meta explicitly brand each as a named holiday category. Diwali was checked particularly thoroughly per instructions: found and evaluated diwali-store, diwali-decoration-items, diwali-gifts, festive-decor, festive-accent, terracotta-festive-decor, golden-peacock-festive-accents, festive-bakeware/-bedding-products/-dinner-products/-furnishing-products/-lights-and-decor/-lights-fbv/-serveware/-table-essentials, gifts-by-festivals. For each candidate, fetched the live PLP, read the 'collection-page-summary-count' element for exact qty, and inspected the actual product slugs on the page (not just the H1/title) to test whether the listed products are genuinely holiday-themed or just generic catalog items re-branded under a seasonal-sounding URL for SEO (a real pattern found repeatedly on this site: several huge collections, e.g. new-year-gifts qty 24708 [~28% of the ~88k-URL product sitemap], diwali-gifts qty 13781, gifts-for-father qty 8305, rakhi-gifts qty 7993, rakshabandhan-gifts-for-brother qty 4828, mothers-day-store qty 1667, rakhi-gifts-hampers qty 960, rakshabandhan-gifts-for-sister qty 10 - all inspected and found to contain generic items with zero holiday-specific character: water bottles, artificial plants, photo frames, wall clocks, showpieces, planters, lamps - i.e. large swathes of the general catalog re-labeled per gifting occasion, not curated seasonal assortments. These were excluded per rules SS5/SS6 (seasonal product type != seasonal category) despite the explicit instruction not to exclude Mother's/Father's Day purely as generic occasions - they were excluded because they fail the genuine-curation/PLP-content test, not because of the occasion type itself. Also excluded as 0-product/broken pages: christmas-table-covers (0), festive-dinner-products (0), festive-lights-fbv (0). Also excluded generic non-holiday-specific 'festive' buckets whose contents showed no seasonal theming on inspection: festive-accent and golden-peacock-festive-accents (multi-faith religious/spiritual idols - Laxmi, Jesus, Om, Ram Darbaar, Makkah Madina - a general Religious & Spiritual category, not one holiday), festive-bakeware (generic cake stands/dough cutters), festive-bedding-products (generic bedsheets/duvets), festive-furnishing-products (generic cushions/throws, one stray Christmas SKU insufficient to qualify the whole category), festive-lights-and-decor (generic candle holders/lamps/lanterns, no holiday markers), festive-serveware (generic platters/trays), festive-table-essentials (generic table linens/coasters). gifts-by-festivals (title 'Gifts By Religious Festivals', meta description spans Diwali, Rakhi, housewarmings AND weddings) was excluded as a mixed multi-occasion marketing/gift-guide hub, not a single-holiday PLP. INCLUDED rows (see rows[]): two Christmas-labeled hubs (Christmas Store, Christmas Gifts) plus three specific Christmas product-type PLPs (Coral Tree Christmas Ornaments, Christmas Ottomans & Pouffe, Christmas Storage Boxes, Christmas Table Runners) whose product slugs are explicitly Christmas-named (baubles, snowmen, christmas cushion covers, candy-cane candles, Rudolph storage jar, etc.); two Raksha Bandhan PLPs (Rakhis, Rakhi Hampers) whose product slugs are genuine rakhi-thread/hamper products (verified distinct, ~40-60% product overlap between the two, not identical listings so both kept). Four brand-specific rakhi-hamper collections (purestory-rakhi, purestory-rakhi-hamper, sowpeace-rakhi-hamper, arte-casa-rakhi-hamper) were found and are genuine rakhi products, but were excluded as they are brand-filtered subsets of the same product TYPE already captured by Rakhis/Rakhi Hampers (sub_category is meant to be product type, not brand), to avoid inflating the row count with near-duplicate brand slices. For Diwali: diwali-store (qty 2575) and diwali-decoration-items (qty 2584) were found to have byte-identical page-1 product listings (diffed the extracted product URLs, zero differences) despite slightly different total counts - treated as the same underlying listing per the shared overlap rule; kept a single row (Diwali Decoration Items, the more complete/specific of the two) and recorded diwali-store as the duplicate alias here rather than as a second row. festive-decor (qty 2373) and terracotta-festive-decor (qty 48) both carry a generic 'Festive' label rather than an explicit 'Diwali' label, but their actual product contents are unambiguous Indian-Diwali vocabulary (urli, toran, oil lamps, diyas, pooja chowki, tealight holders) per rules SS3's own Diwali term list - classified as Diwali and flagged MANUAL REVIEW since the site itself never uses the word 'Diwali' on these two specific pages. Checked and confirmed absent after the full sitemap keyword sweep (3208 collection URLs, zero matches beyond what is listed above): Halloween, Holi, Navratri, Dussehra, Eid, Ganesh Chaturthi, Janmashtami, Pongal, Onam, Durga Puja, Karwa Chauth, Makar Sankranti, Baisakhi, Valentine's Day, Easter, Thanksgiving, St. Patrick's Day, Independence Day, Black Friday - none of these terms appear anywhere in the collections taxonomy. No PDPs were crawled for classification; all decisions made from PLP-level H1/title/meta and the visible product-card grid.
